title: Triangular group coordinates and paired reflection words
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Groups are affine $F$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a,\mathbf G_m$ for [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $G$ be smooth and connected and $T\subseteq G$ a split maximal torus, that is, a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ and maximal among such subgroups. Write $N_G(T)$ for the subgroup functor normalizing $T$ after every scalar extension. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$, paired by $\chi\circ\eta(t)=t^{\langle\chi,\eta\rangle}$. Let $D\subset X\setminus\{0\}$ be finite, nonempty and $\mathbf Z$-linearly independent. For a cocharacter $\eta$, let $U_G(\eta)$ be the subgroup functor of points $g$ for which $\eta(t)g\eta(t)^{-1}$ extends to $t=0$ with value $1$, and let $Z_G(\eta)$ be the subgroup functor centralizing $\eta(\mathbf G_m)$ after every scalar extension. Let $U,V\subseteq G$ be smooth connected unipotent subgroups normalized by $T$, where unipotent means that geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Suppose multiplication $V\times T\times U\to G$ is an open immersion, $Z_G(\lambda)=T$, $U_G(\lambda)=U$ and $U_G(-\lambda)=V$ for some $\lambda\in Y$ with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle=n>0$ for all $\alpha\in D$. For each $\alpha$ suppose given $T$-normalized subgroups $U_\alpha\subset U$ and $V_\alpha\subset V$, with isomorphisms from $\mathbf G_a$ on which conjugation by $T$ scales the parameter by $\alpha$ and $-\alpha$, respectively. Suppose these subgroups generate $U$ and $V$ as closed subgroups. For each $\alpha$ let $n_\alpha\in N_G(T)(F)$ conjugate $U_\alpha$ onto $V_\alpha$ and act on $X$ by $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,c_\alpha\rangle\alpha$, where $c_\alpha\in Y$ and $\langle\alpha,c_\alpha\rangle=2$. Assume that whenever $\eta\in Y$ has $\langle\beta,\eta\rangle\ge0$ for all $\beta\in D$, conjugation by $\eta$ extends to an action of the multiplicative monoid $\mathbf A^1$ on $U$. For each $\alpha$ choose $\eta_\alpha\in Y$ with $\langle\alpha,\eta_\alpha\rangle=0$ and $\langle\beta,\eta_\alpha\rangle=m_\alpha>0$ for every $\beta\ne\alpha$. Suppose evaluation at zero is a homomorphism $p_\alpha:U\to U_\alpha$ restricting to the identity on $U_\alpha$, with smooth connected kernel $K_\alpha$, $U=U_\alpha\ltimes K_\alpha$, $C_U(\eta_\alpha)=U_\alpha$, and $n_\alpha K_\alpha n_\alpha^{-1}=K_\alpha$. Let $W\subset\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be generated by the $s_\alpha$ and put $R=\{w\alpha:w\in W,\alpha\in D\}$. A triangular reflection datum is a tuple of precisely these groups, inclusions, choices, pairing and hypotheses. The torus conjugation action is the actual restricted adjoint action and stability is [def-sfb-torus-character-tangent-weights]. The split torus and maximality use [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology], geometric matrix unipotence uses [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], and the additive copy of the actual character group uses [def-sfb-trivial-torus-coherent-data]. Use the normalizer, cocharacters, image subgroups and Laurent-coordinate evaluation of [def-sfb-rank-one-root-interfaces]. The centralizer $Z_G(\eta)$ is the scheme-theoretic centralizer of the image of $\eta$ in [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]; $U_G(\eta)$ is spelled out on every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ as the points $g$ with a morphism $q:\operatorname{Spec}A\times\mathbf A^1\to G$ restricting on $\operatorname{Spec}A\times\mathbf G_m$ to $\eta(t)g\eta(t)^{-1}$ and with $q(-,0)=1$; points of $\mathbf G_a$ are given by substitution in its polynomial coordinate [def-sc-gm-ga]. Each reflection is identified with precomposition by the inverse of the actual conjugation automorphism of T. Define the paired word subgroup as the subgroup generated by $(n_\alpha,s_\alpha)$ in $G(F)\times\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf Z}(X)$; its elements are precisely the simultaneous evaluations of words in the specified generators and their inverses. Define conjugate subgroup points by $g_A H(A)g_A^{-1}$, closed generation by the smallest-closed-subgroup universal property, and a monoid extension by a scheme morphism $\mathbf A^1\times U\to U$ with the multiplicative monoid action laws restricting to conjugation. Define the rational root space as the $\mathbf Q$-span of $1\otimes R$ in $\mathbf Q\otimes_{\mathbf Z}X$.
